title: Interview readiness, including AI-assisted rounds
goal: Turn knowledge into performance: solve problems under time pressure, narrate your reasoning, run a system design conversation, and work with an AI assistant without handing it the thinking.

steps.title: Algorithm templates
steps.note: Know these cold so you spend interview time on the problem, not on boilerplate.

steps.title: Hiring market findings
steps.note: Re-read the interview section so you know the formats you may meet.

steps.title: Meta's AI-enabled coding interview: how to prepare (Hello Interview)
steps.note: A detailed account of the phases and what interviewers look for. Formats change, so confirm with the recruiter.

steps.title: NeetCode roadmap
steps.note: A topic-ordered problem list for interview-style practice.

steps.title: AI-collaboration drill
steps.brief: Solve 10 problems with an AI assistant under three rules: say your approach aloud first, ask the AI for one small piece at a time, and review and test every suggestion before keeping it. Keep a log of what the AI got wrong.
steps.deliverable: A written log of 10 sessions with the approach you chose, the AI's mistakes you caught and what you would do differently.

steps.title: Ten mock interviews
steps.brief: Complete 10 timed mocks: 5 coding without AI, 3 system design and 2 AI-assisted coding. Record yourself, then review the recordings for silence, unclear reasoning and untested code.
steps.deliverable: A table of the 10 mocks with the main weakness found in each and the fix you practised afterwards.

exit: You solve a new medium problem in 35 to 45 minutes while explaining your reasoning aloud.
You can run a 45-minute system design conversation from requirements to bottlenecks without prompts.
In an AI-assisted drill you state the plan before prompting and catch at least one AI error per session.
You can tell a 90-second story about a project: the problem, your decision, the trade-off and the result.
